_readme: Each dish defined as a typical home-cooked recipe: one serving, broken into base ingredients + grams. An ingredient entry is either a plain number (fixed grams of that exact ingredient) or an object describing a swappable role: {"role": "<label>", "options": [...], "default": "<ingredient_id>", "grams": N} picks one specific default ingredient, while {"role": "<label>", "options": [...], "blend": [...], "grams": N} averages across the blend list when no specific option is named (used for chicken roast, where a generic 'quarter' with no cut specified is genuinely a mix, not one true default). 'portion_presets' (optional) maps a size name to its total gram weight, letting one dish support multiple real portion sizes (e.g. pizza slice size, chicken roast quarter/half/full) instead of guessing one fixed weight. build_dishes.py resolves all of this into per-100g values plus the default serving.
